observations: Veritas sewing machine mounted on a white treadle stand.
Brand 'veritas' is clearly visible in gold lettering on the front panel in photo 1.
Model 'programm automatic' is printed on the right side of the machine body in photo 1.
A black external motor is attached to the rear of the machine with a power cord visible in photo 1.
A piece of white fabric with various decorative and straight stitches is under the presser foot in photo 1.
The stand features a manual foot pedal (treadle) in photo 0.

claims.claim: Heavy duty semi industrial sewing machine

risks.risk: The electric motor or foot controller may be non-functional.
risks.proof: A video of the machine sewing using the electric motor.

risks.risk: Internal mechanical timing or tension issues not visible in a static photo.
risks.proof: A video of the machine sewing through four layers of fabric without skipping stitches.

proof_requests: Video of the machine running under its own motor power.
Close-up photo of the motor's data plate to check wattage.
Photo of the underside/shuttle area to check for rust or lint buildup.
response.reason: The brand and model are clearly identified. The machine is a vintage domestic model, and while the motor is unproven, the item can be priced as a manual machine in its current state.
